chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not belittle what is beneficial on the Day of Judgment, nor belittle what is harmful on the Day of Judgment. So be among that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed you of, like those who witnessed it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.عَايَنَ: To witness with the eyes / to see directly

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to not belittle small deeds in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, underscores the principle of 'tawqif' (divine specification) regarding the weight of deeds, emphasizing that no action is too minor to be accounted for. It calls for 'yaqin' (certainty), urging believers to internalize the reality of the unseen so deeply that their spiritual perception mirrors direct observation, a concept central to Shia eschatology.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Hakeyn, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not belittle what would benefit on the Day of Judgment, nor belittle what would harm on the Day of Judgment. Thus, you should become, regarding whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Informed you all, like the one who can visualise it’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from those whom has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘What is beneficial on the Day of Judgment is not small (insignificant) and nor what is harmful for one on the Day of Judgment is small (insignificant). About whatever Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has informed, you must be like one who has eye-witnessed them.’”
